title: Avoid Using Standard Tees for Back-to-Back Drainage
description: A frequent mistake in waste pipe installation is connecting opposing fixtures with a standard double sanitary tee on a horizontal run or improper back-to-back setup. When wastewater flows from one side, a flat tee can cause water and solid waste to cross over into the opposing pipe rather than directing flow downward into the stack. This cross-discharge leads to frequent clogs, sluggish drainage, and potential back-siphonage. Always use approved double combination fittings or double wyes designed to sweep flow smoothly in the direction of drainage, following your local plumbing code guidelines for proper fitting selection.

Avoid Using Standard Tees for Back-to-Back Drainage

A frequent mistake in waste pipe installation is connecting opposing fixtures with a standard double sanitary tee on a horizontal run or improper back-to-back setup. When wastewater flows from one side, a flat tee can cause water and solid waste to cross over into the opposing pipe rather than directing flow downward into the stack. This cross-discharge leads to frequent clogs, sluggish drainage, and potential back-siphonage. Always use approved double combination fittings or double wyes designed to sweep flow smoothly in the direction of drainage, following your local plumbing code guidelines for proper fitting selection.
